items.prompt: What is the imperative of this verb?
items.explanation: Drop the tāʾ, end in sukūn, and put a hamza in front with the ḍamma of the ʿayn: unṣur.

items.prompt: Why does this imperative begin with a kasra?
options: Because the ʿayn of taḍribu has a kasra
Because every imperative begins with i
items.explanation: The hamza takes a ḍamma when the ʿayn of the present tense has one, and a kasra otherwise.

options: The person spoken to, in six forms
items.explanation: The imperative is made from the second person: two masculine forms, two feminine, and the dual.
